speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; could you describe the specific feeding difficulties your 8-month-old is experiencing and when the abdominal distension first began?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to know if the baby is passing stool or gas, and whether they have had any vomiting. Have you noticed if the vomit is green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby pass any stool or gas, and has the stool ever looked pale or clay-colored? Also, can you describe the color of the urine and whether it is dark or tea-colored?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
